_about: The original's earthquake: EarthquakeGenerator, the one camera shake that every
startEarthquake call in the script feeds, and every call site whose event the port's
simulation already has. Decoded from android_game.bin through the remake's asbc listing
run's decode D11 and its independent check D11_check (which wins where they differ), and
measured on the original's footage (L1 4-29, F14 3-16, F16 4-32). Step 121 of
PRESENTATION ONLY. The class calls AddToCameraPos and nothing else: it moves the drawn
camera for one frame and no body, timer or test the port simulates. The portal manager
maps a tap BEFORE the generator runs (PortalManager::update 138545..139692 #3-4 and #59,
then g_earthquakeGen at Game::preLoop #272-279), so a portal tap lands where it would at
rest, and the port's pointer mapping keeps the rest camera for the same reason.

_source: ONE INSTANCE: g_earthquakeGen, made by a global initialiser (Game.angelscript, bytes
306697..306756, #1-5) and updated as a controller after the camera's and the portal
manager's and before the sky's (Game::preLoop 112536..114414, #272-279).
THE CONSTRUCTOR (109623..109772): earthquake 0 (#1-3), lastTremble 0 (#5-7),
trembleInterval 70 (#9-11, RAW SetV4 70, an integer), eqForth TRUE (#13-15, RAW SetV1 1)
- forth_first - and backValue 0 (#17-19).
startEarthquake(float force) (110309..110425): #3-8 g_scale.scale(force) x 0.35 (MULIf
0.35f) - force_scale; #10-16 min(that, 50f) then max(0f, ...) - cap_px; #18-19
earthquake = that. It OVERWRITES the amplitude: it does not take the larger of the old
and new, and it touches neither eqForth, backValue nor lastTremble.
update() (109902..110265): due when GetTime() - lastTremble >= trembleInterval (#9-19,
TNS) and the amplitude is not 0 (#3-8). FORTH (#28-40): AddToCameraPos(vector2(0,
earthquake)) - y only, the camera DOWN, so the scene moves up on the screen - and
backValue = earthquake. BACK (#49-62): AddToCameraPos(vector2(0, -backValue)), then
earthquake *= 0.5 (MULIf 0.5f) - back_scale, applied on the back alone. Either way
eqForth flips (#42-47, #64-68) and lastTremble = GetTime() (#70-73). Then EVERY frame
(#75-85): abs(earthquake) < 1 (CMPIf 1f) sets it to 0 - stop_px. No x term and no
random draw anywhere in the class (D11_check C8, C9).
THE WRAPPER startEarthquake(float intensity, uint vibrateTime) (337087..337256): #1-4
the call above; #6-21 ForwardCommand('vibrate ' + vibrateTime) when it is above 0,
which is Android's vibrator and draws nothing. The desktop port has none, so each row's
vibrate figure below is recorded in its _source and played by nothing.
_screen_px_per_unit: cap_px and stop_px are BARE literals in raw screen pixels, and force x 0.35 goes through
g_scale.scale, whose m_scaleFactor is GetScreenSize().y / 256 (00_order 8.12a). So the
amplitude is 0.35 x intensity LEVEL units on any screen, and the cap and the stop are
50 / s and 1 / s units, s being the screen's pixels per unit. The port takes the 720 px
screen of the owner's standing ruling R12, 720 / 256 = 2.8125 (art.json depth.scale_factor,
and step 86's reading of a bare literal), extended here from depths to pixel amounts as
D11 section 7 asks the step to say: the cap is 17.78 u and the stop 0.356 u. On a 1080 px
screen the original's would be 11.85 u and 0.237 u, and some shakes would run a pair
longer (D11_check C13); the footage is all 720p.
_clock: WALL-CLOCK milliseconds, and nothing on the controllers' path tests the pause, so a
running shake plays out under a pause (D11_check C10). The port's clock is its layer
clock, which advances by the fixed tick on every tick a level is shown - a pause, a
popup and the end screens included - so it plays out under a pause too, and a tremble
is due on every 5th tick at 60 Hz (83.3 ms), as the original's is on every 5th frame at
60 fps. The original's lastTremble starts at 0 on a clock that is seconds old by the
first level, so its first call is always due at once; the port's starts due.
_state: One generator for the whole game: LoadScene builds a new scene on the same script
module and never rebuilds it (ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:570-613; D11_check C3), so a
running shake, its saved back value and its phase carry across a restart and into the
next level. The port keeps it the same way. Whether it should be reset at a load is LEFT

_when: Where each call lands against the generator's update in the original's frame
(ETHScene::Update, Scene/ETHScene.cpp:458-497; D11 section 1d): the physics step with
its begin-contact callbacks first, then the callbacks of DYNAMIC entities, then the
script loop's controllers in the order Game::preLoop added them, then the callbacks of
STATIC entities. So a contact callback, a dynamic entity's callback and a controller
added before g_earthquakeGen call BEFORE its update (before_update), and trembles the
same frame when it is due; the game-state controller (added after it, #289-297) and a
static entity's callback call AFTER it (after_update), and tremble the next frame at
the earliest. static is read from each caller's .ent (<Entity static=...>).
Within one side the port calls in its own order, the original's being its scene
walk's; it matters only when two different intensities land on one tick.

no_portal_tap._source: D11 row 2. PortalManager::blockPortalEffects (137862..138545) #109-111, startEarthquake(7, 40) - the 40 a vibrate the desktop port has no motor for - with red_waves.ent at the tap (#113-133), on every tap of a level whose budget is 0 while its no_portal_sign exists (placement.json no_budget): 1-15, 2-07, 2-28. PortalManager::update is a controller that runs BEFORE the generator (D11_check C31), so it trembles on the tap's own frame when one is due. Wired in step 123 (the visuals plan's 10.1) on the port's own refusal of such a tap: a picture and a shake, not gameplay.

shot_failed_in_field._source: D11 row 14. ETHCallback_projectile (358053..359141) #211-215, startEarthquake(5, 0), with portal_fail_in_antiportal.ent (#216-232), when a willDie shot arrives with its position inside an antiportal field; a plain portal_fail (#237-257) has none. projectile.ent static 0: a dynamic entity's callback, before the update. Wired in step 123 on the port's own failures that end inside a field it plays (Portals::State::failures): a shot refused where it arrives, or one a body stops inside a field. MEASURED on F3 #161-171: dy -5, +5, -2, +2, -1, +1 px, dx 0.

_not_wired: The 31 CALLs of the global (D11 section 4, D11_check C37-C38) less the 23 wired above
(27 rows: row 1 has two intensities, and row 5 - explode - four callers of its own). Rows 2,
6 and 14 were wired by step 123 (the visuals plan's 10.1) on the refusal and the failures
the port ALREADY plays. Row 3 (a shot killed by an anti_portal_agent in flight, with
antiportal_explosion.ent) waits on R23: the port plays the agent as a no-portal zone and
kills no shot on it, and its picture is 00_order 8.13's unowned row. Rows 4, 8, 10 and 25 (every player, stone and minion impact, 0.6 / 2 / 0.8 x
hitIntensity, and a stone crushing a minion) need a contact's approach speed, which the
engine's PhysicsSystem::Contact does not report and the port can compute itself - the
body's pre-step velocity dotted with the contact normal, with no engine change (D11_check
C48); candidate owner 11.1, which owns the stone rows' pictures. Row 21 (a burned
carranca) and row 30 (4-01's rocket) need systems the port does not have; row 13 (shaker)
is placed by no level. Row 9 is wired for THROWN stones only: the port's Launchers never
culls 3-20's placed stone on its destroyier (Launchers.hpp), so that one never shakes.
